Attack launch overhead on the small-matrix shapes (n=32 B=20, n=176 B=40, n=352 B=40) where geqrf's per-matrix serialization starves the GPU. Write a fused Triton kernel assigning ONE program/CTA per matrix that runs the unblocked Householder loop entirely on-chip: stream column panels through shared memory/registers, compute each reflector and apply it in place, emit (H,tau) for the whole batch in a single launch. Size the on-chip working set to the ~228KB SMEM limit (keep only the active panel resident, never the full matrix) and fall back to torch.geqrf for any n that does not fit.

Panel kernel skips fully-finished trailing tiles (loop starts at tile holding col k+1), halving avg trailing HBM work. ns>1 pipelining OOMs/regresses. n=176:1177us(13.1x), n=352:7850us(4.9x). Geomean 64683us (1.795x). All guards CLEAN.

Attacked the 3 small shapes with fused one-CTA-per-matrix Triton (single launch, no per-matrix geqrf serialization). Two kernels: (1) n=32 register-resident full-tile -> 16.6us (17x over geqrf); (2) n=176,352 HBM-resident PANEL kernel (CTA walks one column + trailing column-tile per step, only active panel resident) -> n=176 1177us (13x), n=352 7850us (4.9x). All other n (512/1024/2048/4096 + off-grid) route to torch.geqrf; all 3 guards + kernelguard + banned-construct scan CLEAN; robust across every conditioning case. KEY FINDINGS: (a) the HBM-panel approach crushes the full-register-tile approach for n>=176 (4-5x) because low register pressure -> higher occupancy beats avoiding HBM traffic; (b) an in-place HBM loop-carried dependency across the k-loop is a silent race in Triton -> a per-step tl.debug_barrier fixes it (no speed cost, memory-bound); (c) starting the trailing loop at the tile holding col k+1 (skip fully-masked finished tiles) ~halves trailing HBM traffic (+8%); (d) num_stages>1 pipelining OOMs SMEM (hw limit ~99KB, not 228KB) and regresses; (e) tl.arange requires pow2 so n=352 pads to BLOCK/P=512. CEILING: strict one-CTA-per-matrix is occupancy-bound for B=40 (only 40 CTAs on 188 SMs, ~80% idle); the kernel is ~57% of HBM-bound floor, the gap is occupancy/latency, not tuning (TJ/warps fully swept, current configs optimal). SUGGESTIONS for a follow-up brief: (1) break the occupancy wall with MULTIPLE CTAs per matrix for n=352 (split trailing columns across CTAs with a grid-stride or cooperative sync) -- departs from strict one-CTA but is the only way past ~80% idle; (2) a small panel-block (WY, nb=8-16) update inside the single CTA would raise arithmetic intensity from 0.25 FLOP/byte (memory-bound rank-1) toward GEMM, but overlaps worker-0/2's blocked direction; (3) my n=32/176/352 kernels are independent of the dominant n=512/1024 cells -- trivially combinable with worker-0/worker-2 wins (different n routed to different paths).

VALID FINDING (crossover confirmed): the batched panel+WY+bmm path CANNOT beat torch.geqrf at B=2/B=8, so n=2048/n=4096 stay on geqrf (no regression). Best committed = 2ae1c1b (global best 6631us unchanged; geqrf retained for these two shapes, documented in-code). EVIDENCE: (1) profiled worker-0's blocked path on n=2048 B=8 -> _panel_qr_kernel 91.6% (register-tile (M_POW2 x nb) spills for large m), trailing GEMM only 7%. (2) profiled geqrf-panel+WY-bmm on n=4096 B=2 -> panel geqr2_domino 80%, trailing GEMM+trsm 14%. (3) standalone tall-skinny panel benchmark: torch.geqrf's geqr2_domino is 3-13x FASTER than the custom Triton panel ((2,4096,32): geqrf 435us vs Triton 4469us) -- geqrf is the best available panel factor. (4) full geqrf-panel+WY-bmm across nb 64-1024: PARITY (n=2048 best 1.06x, n=4096 0.95x = slight regression). (5) TF32: does NOT speed geqrf itself; speeds the trailing bmm to n=2048 1.09x / n=4096 1.07x but degrades factor residual ~1000x (2.3 vs 7e-3, passes loose relative tol on dense but risky on ill-conditioned guard cases) and the combined geomean gain is only 1.013x -- not worth the guard risk. ROOT CAUSE: with B=2-8 there is NO batch parallelism; the per-block tall-skinny Householder panel factor (~80-92% of time) is serial/latency-bound per matrix (geqr2 runs ~32 sequential reflectors over up-to-4096 rows at ~9 GFLOP/s, 1000x off peak); the trailing GEMM that blocking accelerates is only 7-14%, so it cannot overcome the panel bottleneck. The FLAT compact-(H,tau) output contract (householder_product consumes n sequential full-length reflectors) forbids the parallel tall-skinny methods (CholeskyQR/TSQR) that WOULD give within-matrix parallelism -- their block-structured reflectors don't map to flat H without an O(n^3) reconstruction. SUGGESTIONS: (a) accept geqrf here -- it is the no-regression frontier for tiny-B large-n; (b) a real win needs a from-scratch tall-skinny Householder kernel that out-pipelines cusolver's geqr2_domino (split M across a single CTA's many warps without spilling, pipeline the ~32 sequential reflectors) -- high effort, uncertain payoff, and even then bounded by the serial reflector latency; (c) if the leaderboard rules tolerate it, a TF32/low-precision panel could help but needs CholeskyQR2-style refinement AND a cheap Householder reconstruction, which is research-grade. (2) The 2-kernel-split fallback only avoids the barrier if it is per-reflector -> ~352 launches at n=352 (launch explosion); a per-BAND 2-kernel split does not add panel parallelism (the panel's 32 reflectors are still one sequential CTA). (3) A redundant-panel + split-trailing cooperative megakernel does NOT speed the panel (every CTA still factors all M rows), loses the trailing to cuBLAS bmm, OOMs SMEM on the [next_pow2(n),nb] tiles (118-184KB > 99KB hw limit), and when forced to fit (G=6, n=176) was both SLOWER (808 vs 573us) and WRONG (band-boundary staleness fres=194). (4) TSQR-style cooperative panels would parallelize across row-bands with only O(bands) syncs, but produce block-structured reflectors that do NOT map to the required FLAT compact-(H,tau) output without an O(n^3) reconstruction (same blocker as the brief-1 large-n cell). (5) torch.geqrf on these small panels is ~12x slower (n=352: 16995 vs 1439us) -- many tiny serialized calls. ROOT CAUSE: the panel bottleneck is its SEQUENTIAL Householder reflectors, each needing a cross-row reduction; parallelizing those across SMs needs a per-reflector cross-CTA sync that is either unsafe (deadlocking barrier) or launch-explosive. The trailing update (the embarrassingly-parallel part) is ALREADY multi-SM via cuBLAS bmm. SUGGESTIONS: (a) accept the 40-CTA panel path as the occupancy frontier for small-batch small-n; (b) the ONLY way past it is a from-scratch cooperative panel that out-pipelines the sequential reflectors WITHOUT a Triton spin-barrier -- would need a working device-side grid sync (CUDA cooperative-groups via load_inline, NOT Triton) and a flat-Householder reconstruction, both research-grade; (c) the fleet's remaining lever is precision (TF32/low-bit panels) on the big-B cells, not occupancy at small n. n=2048/4096 still on geqrf (brief-1).
